model.title: Title VIII Nursing Workforce Reauthorization Act of 2026

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Reported to Senate):

blocks.text: Title VIII Nursing Workforce Reauthorization Act of 2026
This bill reauthorizes through FY2031, revises, and establishes programs that support recruitment, education, retention, and advanced practices of nurses and nursing school faculty.

Specifically, the bill reauthorizes programs within the Health Resources and Services Administration that provide grants to support increased enrollment in nursing education (including for individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds), advanced nursing education and specialized training, nurse retention, and enhanced patient care. The bill also reauthorizes programs that support student loan repayment and scholarships for nurses who agree to work at facilities with critical nursing shortages and nursing faculty who work at accredited schools of nursing.
Also, the bill expands certain grants to include (1) training on the use of new technologies such as telehealth and virtual resources, and (2) care for survivors of sexual assault.

Additionally, the bill temporarily establishes (1) grants to nursing schools for supplementing the salaries of eligible faculty for a period of up to three years to enhance faculty recruitment and retention, and (2) grants to state agencies, nonprofits, and nursing schools for establishing nursing workforce centers and collecting data regarding the nursing workforce.
This bill extends through fiscal year 2031 and updates several federal programs that help nurses and nursing school faculty get trained, hired, and kept on the job. It also adds a few new programs.

The bill continues federal grants run by the Health Resources and Services Administration. These grants help more people enroll in nursing school, including people from disadvantaged backgrounds, and they support advanced nursing education, specialized training, keeping nurses in their jobs, and improving patient care. It also continues programs that help repay student loans and provide scholarships for nurses who agree to work at facilities with serious nursing shortages, and for nursing faculty who teach at accredited nursing schools.
Some existing grants are expanded. They can now pay for training on new technologies such as telehealth and virtual care tools, and for caring for survivors of sexual assault.

The bill also creates two temporary programs. The first gives nursing schools grants to supplement the salaries of eligible faculty for up to three years, to help recruit and keep teachers. The second gives grants to state agencies, nonprofit groups, and nursing schools to set up nursing workforce centers and to collect data about the nursing workforce.
